items.about:
🚀 Associate Director - DeFinitive Talent

I've spent the past 11+ years building high-performing teams, with over 7 years deeply embedded in the the Digital Assets, Blockchain and Web3 ecosystem. From hands-on technical hiring to executive search, I've partnered with companies across Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East to scale teams with precision, pace and market insight.

As the first hire at Spectrum Search, I built the Blockchain division from the ground up, progressing to Head of Blockchain Recruitment and leading a globally focused team. Following this, I founded Web3 Insights: Talent, a specialist recruitment business dedicated to supporting the next generation of Digital Asset and Web3 companies.
Today, as Associate Director at DeFinitive Talent, I specialise in Product recruitment across Digital Assets, Blockchain and the wider Web3 ecosystem, partnering with founders, executives and product leaders to build world-class teams across emerging technologies and financial infrastructure.

My experience spans hiring across:
✅ Product Management & Product Leadership
✅ Blockchain Infrastructure & Protocols
✅ Digital Assets & Crypto Markets
✅ DeFi, Payments & Stablecoins
✅ Exchanges, Custody & Wallet Technology
✅ Tokenisation & On-Chain Financial Products
✅ Engineering, Commercial and Executive Leadership functions

Having built businesses myself, I understand that successful hiring is about far more than filling vacancies. It's about building long-term partnerships, understanding company vision, and identifying the talent that will define the next stage of growth.

Whether you're building your founding product team, scaling a global organisation, or looking for market insight across Digital Assets and Web3, I bring the network, expertise and execution needed to deliver.

Outside of work, you'll usually find me spending time with my two children, managing a local football team, training in the gym, or searching for great food. I'm also passionate about mentoring young people and giving back through volunteer work, because people have always been at the heart of everything I do.

🔗 Let's connect, whether you're hiring, scaling, exploring the market, or simply want to discuss the future of Product within Digital Assets and Web3.

📧 Email: Aaron@definitivetalent.xyz
📱 Mobile: (+44) 0781 469 3957
🐦 X: @Blockchain_Azza
💬 Telegram: @Blockchain_Azza

Welcome to WEB3 INSIGHTS, a podcast series dedicated to exploring the dynamic world of Web3 through engaging conversations with industry leaders. Hosted by Aaron Hayhurst, a seasoned Web3 Recruitment Leader with over five years of experience in hiring global talent for the decentralized landscape, this podcast was born out of a personal mission to deepen understanding in a rapidly evolving field.

Why This Podcast?
Aaron recognized that navigating the complexities of Web3 can be challenging, even for seasoned professionals. Despite his expertise in sourcing top Web3 talent, he felt a strong need to learn more about the intricacies of the industry from the experts themselves. Thus, WEB3 INSIGHTS was created, as a platform for all those looking to expand their knowledge and stay informed about the latest trends and developments in Web3.

About the Podcast:
In each episode, Aaron interviews top figures in the Web3 ecosystem, delving into their roles, insights on the current state of the industry, and the challenges and opportunities they face. While Aaron doesn’t claim to be a Web3 expert, his passion for fostering understanding in this space drives meaningful discussions that benefit both him and his audience.

What You’ll Gain:
- Expert Insights: Learn directly from the pioneers shaping the future of Web3.
- Talent Landscape: Understand the skills and expertise driving innovation in decentralized technologies.
- Informed Community: Join a growing network of professionals eager to navigate the complexities of Web3 together.

Tune in to WEB3 INSIGHTS and expand your knowledge of the Web3 ecosystem, one conversation at a time!

Twitter/X - @Blockchain_Azza
LinkedIn - https://www.linkedin.com/company/web3-insights-podcast-series/
YouTube - https://www.youtube.com/@WEB3INSIGHTSPodcastSeries

After six years in Web3 hiring, I launched this business to solve a simple problem: traditional recruitment doesn’t work for decentralized teams. We offer a modern, contingent or embedded approach designed to power growth at every stage.

experience.description: I am working at the forefront of developing tools and infrastructure for AI agents and next-generation platforms for e-learning, candidate assessment, interview preparation, and competitive programming.

Judge0 started as my hobby project and later became my side hustle. I have successfully bootstrapped Judge0 as a profitable product company throughout these eight years. In August 2024, I started working full-time on Judge0, believing there was a lot more I could do if I invested myself in it like never before.

As a Senior Software Engineer in the AI team, under the supervision of dr. sc. Karlo Knežević, my most notable work includes:
- migration of 1 PB ClickHouse database to the on-prem server,
- deployment and maintenance of the K8s cluster for the AI team.

I have defined new standards, practices, and communication protocols between three different subteams in the AI team: data analytics, data engineers, and ML engineers. These new standards enhanced our data consistency and database security, helped speed up the onboarding of new team members, and helped to grow the team to 16 members.

I was a member of the Analytics and Data Science Team led by Martina Ptiček. During that period, I worked closely with several data analysts and scientists and:
- created a new codebase and infrastructure organization,
- created a new CI/CD pipeline for over 50 data processing services,
- developed various data processing and monitoring services, and
- introduced new services for data analysis and monitoring.

This team changed its name to "AI and Analytics and Information" and is led by dr. sc. Karlo Knežević since Dec 2021. I worked on big data processing and monitoring infrastructure.

During this period, my proactivity and new ideas completely changed how the AI team worked, from writing and executing queries to creating product and business-related dashboards and reports.

I have also set foundations for data engineering in Sofascore and defined precisely what tasks and projects our first data engineer should work on.

In addition to all that, I was also responsible for onboarding and initial mentoring all new team members.

I was under the supervision of Josip Stuhli (CTO), and during that time, I developed a new distributed multi-platform push notification system that improved overall speed and reliability compared to the old one. Sofascore's notifications to all platforms are sent via this system I developed.

As Auditorium's first contractor and consultant, I took on the engineering manager role. I put together and led an amazing team of designers and engineers to develop and launch the first version of Auditorium in late September 2023. My main job was to keep the team cohesive, motivated and focused so we could deliver a fantastic product for hundreds of thousands of users worldwide. I oversaw everything from technical architecture and infrastructure to people and product management. One of my key technical achievements was integrating Judge0 into Auditorium's platform and managing its deployment on our on-premises infrastructure, which led to significant cost savings and speed improvements. My engineering leadership was crucial in bringing Auditorium's vision to life.

I was a member of Gideon Brother's Brain team which at the time was under the supervision of dr. sc. Ivan Švogor. 

My most notable contributions had a company-wide impact:
- created a new CI/CD pipeline that reduced build time by more than 85% and deploy time by more than 70%
- created a Docker development environment for C++ and Python projects that reduced project setup time by 60%
- introduced C++17 and new technologies such as Docker Compose, GitLab CI, and many others
- helped in educating others about C++ and Docker

My other contributions include:
- worked on a multi-agent simulator and implemented simulation reproducibility
- created a ROS node for error detection in a robot

As a member of Microblink's Tools and Infrastructure team, I have developed a scalable neural network web API, developed a text layout engine for structuring unstructured OCR text, wrote tests for neural network layers in Microblink's neural network inference engine, and developed baseline implementation of Winograd’s minimal filtering algorithm.

Jurica Cerovec, Nenad Mikša, and Domagoj Šarić were my mentors and supervisors.

Text layout engine for structuring unstructured OCR text was also a topic of my Bachelor's thesis.
Developed an internal web application for video processing under the supervision of Martin Skec.

As a member of Infinum's Ruby on Rails team, I worked on three projects where one of them had the best code coverage (100%) and code quality GPA (4/4) in our team.

My mentors and supervisors were Jan Varljen, Damir Svrtan and Stjepan Hadjić.
With a team of other student assistants, I organized laboratory exercises for DisCont Mathematics 1 course under the supervision of prof. dr. sc. Neven Elezović.

Developed catalog application for SmartTVs and worked on a puzzle game for Android and PC.

My mentors and supervisors were Veljko Kukulj and Jovica Popović.

publications.title: Robust and Scalable Online Code Execution System
publications.description: In this paper, we present a novel, robust, scalable, and open-source online code execution system called Judge0. It features a modern modular architecture that can be deployed over an arbitrary number of computers and operating systems. We study its design, comment on the various challenges that arise in building such systems, compare it with other available online code execution systems and online judge systems, and finally comment on several scenarios how it can be used to build a wide range of applications varying from competitive programming platforms, educational and recruitment platforms, to online code editors. Though first presented now, Judge0 is in active use since October 2017 and has become a crucial part of several production systems.

items.headline: Senior Vice President Transformation & Business Excellence @ OQ8 | Ex-Aramco Chief Digital Officer | PhD | INSEAD MBA | Strategy | Energy Transition | $1B Value Delivered | Author & Speaker
items.about:
I lead billion-dollar transformations across energy, refining, and industrial platforms. From Shell’s market expansion strategy to Aramco’s downstream digital agenda to OQ8’s enterprise reconfiguration, I’ve spent three decades converting complexity into alignment—bridging people, technology, operations, governance, and capital.

Currently Executive Vice President at OQ8—a JV between Oman’s OQ and Kuwait Petroleum—I oversee a six-pillar mandate covering transformation, corporate planning, risk, sustainability, digitalization, and shareholder engagement. Delivered $102M in verified impact to date (vs. a $77M target), with a transformation pipeline exceeding $880M by 2027.

Previously, as Chief Digitalization Officer at Saudi Aramco Base Oils, I led a $17M ERP overhaul and deployed an $8M Digital Twin ecosystem across core business functions. I also served as PMO for Aramco’s downstream Operational Excellence portfolio, helping deliver over $137M in value. Earlier roles with Petro Rabigh, Shell, Total, and Accenture deepened my command of cross-functional execution, joint venture complexity, and energy transition strategy.

I specialize in enterprise-wide transformation, ESG-aligned governance, digital-industrial reinvention, and multi-stakeholder navigation. Increasingly, I apply AI not as hype, but as infrastructure—embedding intelligence into decision systems, operational analytics, and scenario-based planning. To date, I have led or architected programs generating $1B in measurable value across MENA and Europe.

My academic foundation includes a PhD from EIMT (Strategic Digitalization), an MBA from INSEAD (Strategy & Finance), and dual engineering degrees in mechanical and hydraulic systems.

I lead with modern integrity—comfortable across diverse cultures, disciplines, and boardrooms. I value clarity, accountability, and human depth in all leadership contexts.

Sector Focus: Energy | Downstream Oil | Refining | Petrochemicals | Industrial Transition | ESG
Expertise: Strategy | Transformation | Business Excellence | AI & Digital | Governance | Risk | M&A
Languages: English (native) | French (native) | Romanian (native) | Italian (intermediate)
Board-Ready | EU Citizen | Global Mobility | Author & Speaker

items.headline: Founder & Director of Engineering at Poseidon Robotics | Building Adaptive ROVs for Challenging Subsea  Missions in Ocean Exploration, Oil & Gas, SAR, and Inspections.
items.about:
As a founding member and Director of Engineering at Poseidon Robotics, I'm passionate about revolutionizing the remotely operated vehicle (ROV) market with cutting-edge, 21st-century technology. 

We specialize in small ROVs and accessories designed for reliability, efficiency, and versatility—whether you're in marine research, offshore inspection, aquaculture, or underwater exploration.After years in the ROV industry servicing legacy systems, I knew it was time to innovate. 

Founding Poseidon Robotics wasn't easy: we've logged countless 4,000+ hour years, pulled all-nighters on critical projects, and racked up miles at trade shows and demos all around the world. But those challenges fueled our success. Today, we're a fast growing company, shipping ROVs worldwide, expanding our capabilities, and continuously improving to meet your needs.

Personally, the past four years have been a masterclass in entrepreneurship—I've gained more hands-on expertise in ROV system design, electromechanical integration, power electronics, pressure vessels, and beyond than I could have in decades elsewhere. And we're just getting started: expect even more innovative solutions on the horizon.

If you're seeking high-performance small ROVs or accessories to elevate your operations, let's connect. I'm sharing insights, industry updates, and behind-the-scenes stories here on LinkedIn (and increasingly on X—follow us @PoseidonRobotics for the latest). What challenges can Poseidon Robotics solve for you? Reach out—I'm here to help.

currentPosition.description:
If Poseidon Robotics designed or built it, I had a hand in it.  Working alone or in a small team, this position covers everything technical in a small company.  From initial concept, to system design, critical calculations, Mechanical and Electronic design and simulation, modeling in SOLIDWORKS, part selection and sourcing, schematic capture and board layout (OrCAD), prototyping, first article testing and quality control, qualification testing, documentation, and field trials.  

The job doesn't end there: once a new and better product is created, the hard work of marketing and sales begins.  Working trade shows, answering questions, providing field demonstrations and customer integrations, through to improving customer experience and implementing engineering change orders are all part of the process. 

Once a product becomes popular, the real challenge of scaling production begins.  This involves hiring staff, providing training, manufacturing engineering and new process selection, cost controls, and putting "scalable" processes in place to allow the company to grow from 1 unit to thousands.

items.headline: Co-Founder @ One Horizon | Automating repetitive work so engineers can focus on what matters. Join our beta → onehorizon.ai | Passionate about AI, dev productivity & building tools that actually help teams | Ex-Khoros PM
items.about:
I’m building One Horizon to rethink how engineering teams operate in an AI-native world.

Today, developers spend a significant part of their time navigating tools, chasing updates, and manually stitching together context across Slack, GitHub, Jira, Linear, and meetings. The result: lost focus, hidden blockers, and slower delivery than teams are actually capable of.

At One Horizon, we’re changing that.

We’re building an AI-powered team productivity platform that automatically connects the dots across your workflow. From daily standups and progress summaries to real-time insights on priorities, blockers, and dependencies, our goal is simple: eliminate repetitive work and give engineers back uninterrupted time to build.

I co-lead product, strategy, and execution, working closely with innovative teams across the world to turn real workflow pain into scalable solutions. We’re currently building a Slack-first AI assistant that helps teams start their day with clarity instead of confusion.

Before One Horizon, I spent 4+ years at Khoros as a Product Manager focused on automation and AI. I owned and shipped features across multiple teams in India, Ukraine and the United States, worked directly with global enterprise customers, and helped bring AI-driven products from concept to production. I also built custom prototypes, internal tools, and experiments to accelerate 7-figure deals and validate new ideas, contributing to high-impact enterprise outcomes.

Earlier in my career, I worked hands-on in conversational AI and automation, designing and implementing solutions end-to-end for companies across industries. That foundation still shapes how I build today: close to the user, focused on real problems, and biased toward execution.

What drives me is simple: reducing friction in how teams work. The best teams are not just fast, they are aligned, focused, and operating with clarity. I believe AI can unlock that at a completely new level.

Interested in:
• Connecting with engineers, product leaders, and founders working on developer tools, AI, or productivity
• Sharing ideas on dev workflows, metrics, and scaling engineering teams
• Meeting potential partners and early adopters for One Horizon

If you’re building, scaling, or thinking about the future of engineering teams, let’s connect.

items.about:
Instigate.ai has released a prototype of a media storytelling tool which pushed the envelope - in several directions.

The Tool = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rx-RK3j4rW4

We also have a video explaining our B2B2C DTC Brands Web3 Advertising platform = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bwBkaGKWBg0

Between these two videos, our working code, 2 patents and a trademark, we have experienced software, entertainment and AI execs running Instigate.ai. But this page is about Marc - so let's talk about him (me.)

Marc is an experienced software CEO/Chairman - who co-founded MacroMind, which became Macromedia [MACR.]

Marc Canter is a serial entrepreneur, visionary leader, zero to one expert and opinionated tech evangelist who has been involved in the software industry from the outset in the early 1980's.  His reputation is that of a straight talker, no bullshit advocate of users, user's rights and warrior in the on-going battle between man vs machine.

Marc's company MacroMind was founded in '84 - became Macromedia in '91.  He was one of the founding fathers of the multimedia industry and spent the 90's working on "broadband"​ and "Interactive TV"​ content and tools.  The 00's brought focus on blogging and social media - when Marc founded Broadband Mechanics which sold and licensed a white labeled social networking platform called "PeopleAggregator."​

The 10's saw Marc move his family to Cleveland, Ohio (in 2009), where he founded "Digital City Mechanics"​ - and started working on a system to create on-line jobs and "digital economy ecosystems."​

Instigate, Inc. was created in the summer of '16 and started working on an AI Authoring system which makes training user's own sentient Storytelling Beings possible.

Marc Canter is a 38+ year software entrepreneur focused on leveraging interactive web and mobile based technology with community and people in general.  

Specialties: Toolsmith | software developer | evangelist | visionary | zero to one | user interface & experience expert | standards builder | teacher | mentor | AI expert | entrepreneur | team leader | coder whisperer | Product manager | systems thinker | architect | user advocate.

items.about:
AI Automation Agency Belfast | AI Lean™ • AI 6 Sigma™ • AI Automation • AI Governance • AI Training
I’m Lisa Wallace, Founder of AI For Business Northern Ireland, an AI Automation Agency and AI Training Academy helping businesses in Belfast, Northern Ireland, the UK and beyond use AI to solve real operational problems.
My work combines AI, Lean, Six Sigma, automation, governance, training and operational excellence.
Most businesses know they should be using AI, but they are stuck:
Where do we start?
What is worth automating?
What risks do we need to manage?
What roles will change?
What training do our people need?
That is where my approach is different.
Most AI providers focus on tools.
Most Lean consultants focus on process.
I combine both.
AI Lean™ = streamline workflows, remove waste and improve flow
AI 6 Sigma™ = reduce defects, errors, variation and rework
AI Automation = automate repetitive tasks, speed up delivery and reduce admin
The goal is measurable improvement: time saved, cycle time reduced, throughput improved, admin removed, rework reduced and clearer performance visibility for leaders.
I bring real operational experience from manufacturing, oil and gas, aviation, telecoms, financial services, government and industrial environments, including work with Shell, Bombardier Belfast, FG Wilson, Survitec Group, easyJet, Vodafone, Lloyds Banking Group and Danske Bank.
What AI For Business Northern Ireland delivers:
• AI Audits

I also run Cherry Moon AI, helping women upskill with AI, build confidence, explore creativity and future-proof their careers in a friendly, accessible way.
My mission is to help businesses use AI safely, practically and profitably , to reduce waste, improve flow, automate repetitive work, strengthen governance, prepare for the EU AI Act and make AI useful in the real world.

currentPosition.description:

projects.title: Perimetrix & Argus: Spatial-Vector AI Architecture
projects.description:
Engineered a domain-agnostic hybrid AI architecture using Oracle Database 26ai to solve the false-positive limitations of traditional rule-based geofencing systems. This proof-of-concept natively fuses Oracle Spatial for exact entity containment (SDO_INSIDE, SDO_WITHIN_DISTANCE) and AI Vector Search for behavioral classification (VECTOR_DISTANCE) within a single SQL execution plan. By encoding real-time entity signals into 3-dimensional behavioral vectors, the system accurately scores complex behaviors against reference patterns, such as distinguishing a "Safe Traffic Detour" from "High Risk Loitering". The architecture successfully demonstrates reusable vector feature engineering across both outdoor GPS tracking and indoor sensor grids.

Repository: https://github.com/ddrechse/Perimetrix

projects.title: Schema GraphRAG: Enterprise NL2SQL Demonstration
projects.description:
The official reference implementation of the Schema GraphRAG methodology. This project demonstrates how to solve LLM hallucination in complex, foreign-key-free relational databases (such as Oracle EBS). It utilizes graph analytics and SQL Tuning Set workload intelligence to provide Large Language Models with accurate, structural context, enabling highly reliable Natural Language to SQL (NL2SQL) generation over massive enterprise schemas.

publications.title: The Revolution of Work: Fuck the Patriarchy and the Workplace It Built
publications.description:
This book is the start of a revolution—THE Revolution—to make workplaces and employment better for all humans.

Anessa Fike is tired of seeing the same broken elements in the workplace happening over and over again in a structure set up centuries ago to help only the patriarchy succeed.

The Revolution of Work calls attention to how work isn't working for most people today and how it's all connected to holding up the status quo for the success of one demographic—to the detriment of others. Bringing a wealth of experience from organizations world-wide and sharing her own lived experiences, Fike's writing makes it feel like you are sitting with a friend in deep and meaningful discussion.

If you feel gaslighted, overlooked, or dismissed in the workplace, this book will open your eyes to what happens and what you can do to shift toxic workspaces.

items.about:
I help enterprises become AI‑ready organizations — moving beyond pilots and proofs of concept into trustworthy, compliant, and strategically aligned AI ecosystems.
With 40+ years of global leadership across Canada, the US, the UK, APAC, and the Middle East, I bring the maturity of experience and the precision of an architect. As a Fractional AI Architect and Governance Auditor, I ensure CXOs can drive decision‑critical AI transformations with confidence, clarity, and measurable ROI.
My expertise spans:
AI Governance & Auditing: Embedding oversight to eliminate bias, misalignment, and reputational risk.
Fractional Architecture: Designing scalable AI pipelines that integrate with legacy IT while preparing for agentic automation.
Forward Deployed Engineering [FDE] Practices.
Organizational Role Design: Defining critical roles — AI Strategists, Agentic Architects, Data Engineers, Compliance Analysts, UX Strategists, Sprint Coaches — aligned with processes and guardrails.
Process & Guardrails: Establishing operational guardrails that enforce accountability, escalation paths, and bias detection.
CXO Advisory: Guiding leaders through the ethical, human, and strategic dimensions of AI adoption.
My mission is simple yet uncompromising: to transform enterprises into AI organizations — with the right governance, architecture, roles, and guardrails — so they are resilient, compliant, and future‑ready.

items.about:
Software Engineering Manager and system design leader with 15+ years of experience building scalable software, leading teams, and solving complex backend and data problems.
 
I specialize in software architecture, distributed systems, APIs, databases, performance optimization, and reliable system design. My experience includes leading cross-functional teams, mentoring engineers, and delivering projects across the full software lifecycle, from requirements and prototyping to implementation, testing, and long-term maintenance.
 
I work mainly with C#, Node.js, JavaScript, and Python, with a strong focus on building systems that are simple, resilient, and designed to evolve.
 
I’m especially interested in how AI will reshape software development. The biggest shift is not just faster coding. It is the growing importance of judgment, system design, code review, and engineering clarity in a world where implementation becomes cheaper. As AI changes how software gets built, I believe the engineers who think clearly, design well, and understand trade-offs will stand out even more.
 
I also enjoy helping engineers grow by breaking down complex technical ideas into practical lessons they can apply immediately.

I had the pleasure of working with Raul for two years at ANDMORE (formerly Juniper/IMC). During my time with the company as a QA Automation Engineer, we had the opportunity to collaborate both cross-project as well on the same team, maintaining and expanding our core API functionality. 

I found Raul to be an engaging and professional communicator, his insight and leadership providing welcome guidance to a team of stellar developers. I was constantly impressed by his critical approach to architecture, his focus on leveraging and extending current functionality in response to changing business rules and avoiding needlessly complicated solutions. I found Raul's philosophy to be a refreshing mix of "Keep up to date with current best practices" and "If it aint broke, don't fix it".

As a Software Tester by trade, Raul is my favorite kind of Engineer. Always willing to discuss the code base, what/why certain changes were made, and what the future is likely to hold. Not one to simply "throw the PR over the fence", he views QA as a necessary part of the development process which makes our process much more effective. Raul's leadership on a team not only elevates the effectiveness of his direct reports but improves the day-to-day of everyone involved in the software development lifecycle.

I found Raul to be an absolute joy to work with and wholeheartedly recommend him to any team with a need for top notch talent.

items.about:
Leveraging ten years steering pharmaceuticals, chemicals, food and automotive projects, I fuse hands-on engineering depth with board-level clarity to turn greenfield visions into safe, profitable reality. I have guided €18 M CAPEX builds, led crews of 62, safeguarded 150+ GMP clean-room assets, and generated seven-figure savings through vendor strategy and ERP-driven maintenance. My toolkit spans concept, BIM design, procurement, construction, commissioning and lifecycle reliability; my ethos—rigor, speed and transparent stakeholder dialogue—keeps lines humming while budgets stay intact.

Previous positions held: Project Manager / Maintenance Manager / Piping Team Leader / Project Engineer

Below are some of the key accomplishments that I have attained:
• Supervised three flagship battery, electronics and automotive factories from design through handover, all on schedule. - (JFES Ltd.)
• Ensured the operation of ~150 pieces of cleanroom equipment - (Béres Pharmaceuticals Plc.)
• Cut €1.8 M from a €3.8 M spares budget by renegotiating 3 000+ items for 463 rotating machines. - (KALL Ingredients Ltd.)
• Procured and installed 171 process units (€4 M) inside a chemical plant, achieving first-pass start-up. - (K&PChem Ltd.)

My mother has a degenerative disease called Post Polio Syndrome.  She's had mobility issues since the age of 17 months old.  Just before the pandemic got started... She fully lost mobility in her lower extremities.  

I moved her into my home and provide in-home care while working remotely in the time that I have left in the day, & night where needed.  Lucky to have the extra room in the house, & to have her near to take care of.  It does limit my travel options and commuting for a regular work commitment.  

Family is the most important thing!  She now works as CFO of CCC  (She relaxes!)

Not many people care or consider how much time it takes to feed, bath, & care for a person that can barely move.   I'm grateful to able to care for her, as she did for me, but it does hurt my ability to work onsite anywhere, because of the variation and flexibility of her needs.

My father passed away when I was 7 years old, I owe him this, so I never waver.  My mom is awesome, and family values are way more important than the corporate values that lay people off for profit.  Family first, and #lovemore.

items.headline: Software Engineer at GeoWise AI
items.about:
I'm Youssef, a Technical Project Manager and Full-Stack Software Engineer, a Senior UI/UX designer, a professional QA tester, and a developer. I design, build, and scale production-grade digital products, either by leading cross-functional teams or executing the full stack myself.
 
I work alongside a professional QA tester (Merna) on every project, ensuring every release meets production-grade quality standards before it reaches the client.
 
From brand strategy and interface design to frontend engineering, backend architecture, and deployment, I ensure every layer is aligned, scalable, and built for real-world use.
 
With a background in Business Administration and digital marketing, I approach products beyond code. I focus on how they are positioned, experienced, and how they drive measurable business value.
 
What sets me apart
 
I engineer production AI systems end to end, architecting retrieval pipelines, agent orchestration, and evaluation logic for RAG workflows, voice and conversational agents, and automation, working AI-native throughout the build with Cursor, Claude, and Codex under my own architectural decisions and code review.
 
I build AI agents focused on outcomes. From lead qualification to automated telebooking, follow-ups, and full user journey handling, these systems are designed to increase conversion, reduce manual workload, and streamline operations at scale.
 
My hybrid experience allows me to:
 Design high-impact UI/UX and build fast, performant frontends
 Architect and integrate scalable backend systems and APIs
 Launch full-stack web and mobile products from concept to production
 Build clean CI/CD pipelines and manage deployment workflows
 Design and deploy AI systems that enhance product intelligence and automate business processes
 
I work within agile environments using tools like ClickUp and Jira to maintain clarity and speed. I also keep a dedicated QA tester on every engagement, funded from my own pocket, so clients get full test coverage without an added line item on their invoice.
 
My marketing background still shapes how I think. Every feature, interaction, and design decision must solve a real problem and support business growth.
 
 In short words:
 A full-stack engineer who delivers production-ready systems fast
 A designer who understands both user experience and business impact
 A developer who connects frontend experience with backend logic
 A project lead who bridges technical execution and business strategy
 Someone who can design and deploy AI systems that actively drive conversions and automate operations

items.about:
Empowering Electronics Manufacturers with DFM-Driven, Fast-Turn PCB & PCBA Solutions， electronic design.
With over 30 years of experience in iurnkey OEM/ODM, Contract Manufacturing, we help electronics manufacturers, EMS providers, and electronics design companies bring complex products to market faster through DFM-focused PCB fabrication, advanced PCBA assembly, and fast-turn production — with no MOQ.
Our work is centered on one core value:
turning complex designs into manufacturable, reliable, and cost-effective PCB & PCBA solutions.
What we Do & Who I Support
At djt-e, we provide one-stop PCB & PCBA services, covering design support, fabrication, and assembly.
We specialize in high-mix prototypes, small-to-medium batch production, and high-difficulty PCBA manufacturing, where engineering experience and process control truly matter.
Our key technical capabilities include:
HDI PCBs & high-layer count boards
Rigid-Flex & Flexible PCBs
High-speed & high-frequency PCBs
Gold finger, thick copper & thick gold boards
Blind / buried vias and depth-controlled routing
We support customers in automotive electronics, medical devices, industrial control, aerospace, robotics, and consumer electronics, serving markets across Europe, North America, and Oceania.
How I Add Value
We work closely with customers from the early design and DFM stage, helping identify manufacturability risks before they impact cost, yield, or delivery.
By using tools such as CAM350 and Genesis, I provide practical DFM recommendations to:
optimize stack-up and impedance control
improve yield and assembly reliability
reduce production cost
shorten lead time and avoid re-spins
Whether it’s fast-turn prototypes, no-MOQ pilot runs, or stable mass production, I help ensure projects move forward efficiently — from design release to final delivery.
Why Clients Choose djt-e
Engineering-Driven Manufacturing: Not just build-to-print, but DFM-supported solutions
Fast Delivery & No MOQ: Ideal for NPI, prototypes, and agile product development
Advanced Capabilities: HDI, rigid-flex, high-speed & complex PCB structures
Certified Quality Systems: ISO9001, ISO14001, IATF16949, UL
Proven Global Trust: Serving 4,000+ customers worldwide
Products & Services
PCB Fabrication (Prototype to Mass Production)
PCBA Assembly (SMT / THT / Turnkey)
HDI, Rigid-Flex, Flex & Multilayer PCBs
High-Speed & High-Frequency PCBs
Metal Core & Special Process Boards

items.headline: 12 years scaling AdTech, OTT and FinTech | Shipped RTB systems, payment infrastructure (PSO-licensed), and OTT platforms serving millions | PHP · Java · Spring Boot · Node.js · Kubernetes · AWS
items.about:
12 years building backends that hold up under real-world load — real-time bidding at Eskimi, OTT streaming for millions of viewers at Bongo, and payment infrastructure at PayBuddy that earned a PSO license from Bangladesh Bank.

I'm a backend engineer and architect who's spent his career in the hard parts of software: low-latency systems, regulated environments, and the long monolith-to-microservices migrations most teams avoid. I've led engineering across four verticals — AdTech, OTT, FinTech, and luxury e-commerce — and across stacks: Java (Spring Boot), PHP (Laravel/Symfony), Node.js (NestJS), and Python (Flask/FastAPI), all deployed on Kubernetes (EKS) with Terraform-managed AWS infrastructure.

What I'm known for:
Designing systems teams can actually maintain. Migrating production monoliths to microservices using the Strangler pattern — zero downtime, bidirectional sync. Building custom IAM with Keycloak SPIs for multi-device OAuth2. Optimizing ClickHouse and MySQL at the schema level, not just the query level. Standing up RabbitMQ and Kafka pipelines with proper DLQs, retries, and backpressure. Cutting RTB exchange latency where milliseconds translate directly to revenue.

What I do day-to-day:
Currently leading engineering at BluBird Interactive, architecting Chatlei — a multi-tenant unified messaging SaaS on Java 21 + Spring Boot WebFlux, integrated with Meta Graph API across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. Mentoring 10+ engineers, owning SRE responsibilities, and shipping open-source Laravel packages along the way.

How I lead:
I've managed teams of 5–10 engineers. My focus is code review culture, test discipline, and giving juniors enough rope to grow without enough to hang the production database. I write runbooks. I review PRs seriously. I don't ship without observability.

I read technical books, write about infrastructure (recently: Apache Kafka 4.2 in KRaft mode on a $7 EC2), and hold an MBA from North South University alongside Master's and Bachelor's degrees in Mathematics.
Open to: Principal/Staff Engineer, Tech Lead, or Engineering Manager roles — remote or relocation.

Reach me at selimppc@gmail.com.

items.headline: Program Manager at Tata Consultancy Services
items.about:
I am an AI Transformation Leader and Enterprise Modernization Architect with 16+ years of experience delivering large-scale modernization, cloud transformation, and AI-enabled enterprise solutions across the insurance and financial services industry.
 
My career has evolved from deep expertise in mainframe engineering (COBOL, CICS, DB2, JCL, IDMS, PL/I) to leading enterprise modernization initiatives and, more recently, driving AI-powered transformation. I specialize in helping organizations modernize mission-critical legacy platforms while preserving business capabilities and accelerating digital innovation.
 
I have led modernization initiatives across multiple enterprise applications by designing hybrid architectures, API-first integrations, cloud-native services, and AWS-based modernization strategies. My experience spans legacy assessment, business rule mining, reverse engineering, cloud modernization, application decomposition, and enterprise transformation roadmaps.
 
In recent years, I have focused on Generative AI and Agentic AI, leading initiatives that apply AI to legacy modernization, software engineering productivity, incident management, operational intelligence, knowledge management, and business process optimization. I have designed AI-enabled solutions using AWS Bedrock, Databricks AI, Google Cloud AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector databases, and LLM-based enterprise workflows to improve delivery efficiency and accelerate modernization outcomes.
 
I enjoy leading cross-functional global teams across engineering, infrastructure, QA, operations, and business organizations, combining technology leadership with delivery governance to execute complex transformation programs successfully.
 
Core expertise
 
• AI Transformation & Enterprise AI Adoption
 • Generative AI & Agentic AI
 • Enterprise Modernization & Legacy Transformation
 • AWS Cloud Modernization & Hybrid Architecture
 • Mainframe Modernization (COBOL, CICS, DB2, JCL, IDMS, PL/I)
 • Solution Architecture & API Integration
 • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) & AI Knowledge Systems
 • Program Delivery & Technology Leadership
 • Stakeholder Management & Enterprise Consulting
 
I am passionate about helping organizations bridge the gap between legacy systems and AI-driven enterprises, enabling faster modernization, intelligent automation, and sustainable business transformation.

I build high-performing teams, scalable recruitment systems, and people-first operations that help businesses grow.
 
As a Senior Talent Acquisition Manager and HR Business Partner, I specialize in helping startups and growing organizations attract exceptional talent, strengthen people operations, and build scalable HR systems aligned with business growth.
 
My expertise spans Global Talent Acquisition, HR Business Partnering, People Operations, Recruitment Strategy, Employee Relations, Performance Management, Workforce Planning, and AI-driven Process Automation.
 
I have led end-to-end recruitment for technical and non-technical roles across Engineering, Software Development, AI, Product, UI/UX, QA, DevOps, Marketing, Sales, HR, Finance, Customer Success, Operations, and Executive Leadership.
 
Beyond recruitment, I work across the employee lifecycle — including onboarding, engagement, performance management, organizational development, HR reporting, people analytics, and stakeholder management.
 
My operations experience allows me to design scalable workflows, optimize internal systems, establish KPIs, strengthen accountability, and implement AI-powered automation to improve efficiency and execution.
 
I believe great companies are built by combining the right people, the right systems, and the right leadership.

items.headline: Principal Software Engineer
items.about:
Howdy 👋 I consider myself a full stack software engineer who loves picking up diverse technologies and making them work wonders. My current sweet spot lies in using Typescript with Next.js and React, but I'm always eager to expand my tech toolkit.

At the heart of my work philosophy is a love for being part of small, dynamic teams in early-stage startups. I thrive in environments where I can contribute beyond the typical 'developer' role - engaging with all levels of the business to collaboratively build something truly remarkable.

I also dabble in levelling up the teams I work with. Whether it's refining processes or nurturing the growth of individuals and the team as a whole, I love making a positive change that brings out the best in everyone involved.

Currently, I'm embracing a phase in my life where working remotely aligns best with my personal and professional goals. This flexibility allows me to deliver high-quality work while maintaining a balanced lifestyle.

I'm excited to connect with like-minded professionals and organisations that value creativity, collaboration, and a holistic approach to technology and business. Let's explore how we can create something incredible together!

currentPosition.description:
I've been lucky enough to join forces with the puzzling Minute Cryptic team to help bring the wonderfully accessible and inclusive cryptic puzzles to an ever growing audience. This continues to be one of the most fun jobs in my career, working with both an absolutely wonderful team and a warm and friendly community of puzzlers. It's very rare to find the intersection of both, so I consider myself lucky!

I’m currently leading the development of the backend platform along with the website and mobile experiences. While I’m often the one in the weeds across the stack day to day, it’s very much a team effort. I get to build the systems that support a community of hundreds of thousands of solvers, with new puzzlers arriving every day. No two days are the same; one minute I’m tuning SQL and scaling infrastructure, the next I’m shipping mobile improvements, building new puzzle features, tightening up CI pipelines, or integrating with our external community platform, it's the kind of variety that keeps my brain running in all the right ways.

I'm having a go at building Calmly because I wanted to help others access tools and strategies for meaningful reflection on their work life. I'm hoping to empower others to develop emotional self-awareness and enhance their stress resilience, ultimately creating a better, more balanced work experience.

If this sounds interesting - I'd love to hear from you! Please reach out and let's have a chat.

• Launched Calmly, a platform designed to enhance emotional self-awareness and stress resilience, starting as a Slack bot before pivoting to a web app for broader accessibility.

• Overcame the challenge of routing messages between a React frontend and an asynchronous Slack backend by building a state machine for contextual chatbot responses and a messaging system atop Postgres using pg-boss.

• Iteratively enhanced features based on direct user feedback (emails, video calls, Slack chats), resulting in a product pivot to a web app that simplified onboarding and expanded the user base.

• Developed a smart journaling platform with an AI-driven review loop that summarises user journal entries and enables contextually aware conversations about specific entries.

Amber acquired my previous company, Powerpal at the start of 2023,  and I eventually made my way across into a Staff Engineer position within the Amber team. Amber is an innovative wholesale energy retailer, that offers consumers direct access to wholesale electricity rates and also provides smart solutions for solar and battery automation to maximise cost savings and enhance home electricity management.

During my time with the Amber team, I worked in and leading the Product Growth stream. My main focus was on driving new customer registrations, promotion management and refining the onboarding process to ensure a seamless introduction to Amber's services.

Some highlights from my time at Amber:

  • Directly drove 5% of Amber's new customer acquisition by developing a system within the Powerpal app that allows customers to preview their electricity costs with Amber’s wholesale pricing model, giving them a tangible sense of what switching could mean for their electricity bills.

  • Initiated and drove customer feedback efforts to gauge sentiment throughout the onboarding journey. This feedback helped us identify highly satisfied customers, which drove additional  and encourages them to share their positive experiences, thereby organically boosting our reputation.

  • Lead a team responsible for building and maintaining Amber's quoting system and partner channels. I also helped the team focus on continual enhancements to the customer onboarding process to streamline user experience and engagement.

I was a Principal Software Engineer at Powerpal, where we pioneered the field of home energy monitoring. It was an exhilarating experience melding innovation with practicality to make energy management both smart and user-friendly.

During my tenure, I loved tackling challenges and pushing the limits of what we could achieve in smart home technology in our very small but mighty team. Here are some of the highlights from my time there:

  • Led the development of the Powerpal app, which now helps over 250,000 Australians keep track of their energy use. My focus was on making energy monitoring straightforward and insightful.

  • Developed a cutting-edge booking automation system that contacted leads via SMS, optimized installers' routes, and kept customers in the loop. This tool reduced a full-time scheduling task to just a few hours a week, boosting our operational efficiency significantly.

  • Enhanced the Powerpal platform to provide customized energy-saving tips, detailed insights, and personalized offers based on individual usage patterns. This initiative empowered our users to make more informed energy choices.

  • Oversaw product development from concept to completion. I guided our talented team through intricate projects, ensuring we consistently hit the mark with high-quality, engaging solutions.

  • Developed a custom IoT system to complement our mobile app, involving hands-on work with hardware and firmware specs, and building a robust backend with AWS IoT to manage thousands of devices.

  • Dipped my toes into marketing by automating our Facebook ad campaigns, which dynamically generated and adjusted ads based on installation schedules and targeted strategies.

Once the project team I was a part of had successfully built and rolled out the first iteration of Blueshifts next-generation system, I set my sights on improving the broader engineering team. I worked closely with Blueshift's senior management to flesh out how to best lead the growing technology teams. After many iterations and getting buy in from the wider group, a new way to work and set of teams emerged. I then stepped into a leadership role in one of the new teams and built out a highly functioning group of technologists that valued a growth mindset and high levels of friendly collaboration to delivery outstanding solutions.

Some highlights from this role:

  • Created a high trust environment where everyone felt safe to voice their thoughts and ask for help when needed. The level of psychological safety lead to a team that could identify its strengths and weaknesses and improved upon them day by day

  • Improved the output of the team by focusing engineering efforts on reducing technical debt and automating many of the manual processes that were in place

  • Grew the broader engineering team by acting as an internal technical consultant and helping to upskill the wider organisation and drive best practice throughout Blueshifts systems

After working in the finance industry for almost a decade, I was looking for something a bit different and exciting, and Blueshift offered me just that. Blueshift is an SMB company based on the Central Coast of NSW that specialises in Integrated Business Planning, incorporating Trade Promotion Management (TPM), Demand Forecasting, Joint Business Planning and Business Intelligence. They were in the process of building their next-generation micro-service based system to help deliver a solution that performs at scale, and I joined the team to give a helping hand.

Some highlights from this role:

  • Created a more scalable system architecture by applying techniques derived from DDD (Domain Driven Design), CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) and Event Sourcing

  • Improved the quality of software by driving initiatives around unit testing, clean code, developer collaboration and 'share and learn' sessions

  • Enabled the viability of spinning up and down client instances in the cloud quickly and easily by introducing infrastructure as code tooling to the team (Terraform and Ansible)

  • Reduced system management overhead by configuring and deploying several on premise multi-node MemSQL and Kubernetes clusters to support both our internal and client facing workloads

I was looking to extend my knowledge in the “DevOps” space, and this role gave me the perfect opportunity to do just that. The main goal of this position was to help facilitate the development team to move towards a continuous delivery and deployment culture.

Some highlights from this role:

  • Reduced time to troubleshoot system issues by setting up an ELK stack to aggregate logging from multiple services

  • Empowered development teams to move towards a DevOps culture by setting them up with a Docker based build, test and deployment pipelines that gave them more confidence to release and deploy changes faster

  • Made Optivers infrastructure more flexible by migrating services hosted on physical servers into AWS using Terraform and Ansible to create a consistent and automated process

After working my way up to become a senior developer in my team, I became very interested in moving into a leadership position. So, when the opportunity to lead a team presented itself, I jumped at it. I went on to lead the team of 10 developers to design and develop new middle office and finance applications to facilitate ASIA Pacific wide reconciliation, profit and loss report generation and profit and loss attribution.

Some highlights from this role were:

  • Renewed confidence in the core product with Optivers CFO and the business by working closely with both sides to identify a true minimal viable product and put a consistent and predictable agile delivery method in place

  • Greatly improved the morale and output of team members by promoting a growth mindset and empowering them to drive their ideas forward

  • Created a much higher alignment and collaboration between the development team and our business units by unifying everyone under a single physically co-located group, enabling multiple interactions every day

I joined Optiver as a junior developer and quickly fell in love with my job. Early on, I dedicated myself to understanding the intricacies of the business, which allowed me to take ownership of several key products utilized by our internal market risk, middle office, and finance teams. This experience proved very useful in shaping me into becoming a well-rounded developer, adding value at all levels of the software development process.

Some highlights from this position were:

  • Reduced the generation of complex market risk exposure reports from over 1 hour to less than 1 minute through a combination of local optimisation and improving the upstream data transfer protocols

  • Improved the quality and delivery rate of UI applications by moving the team from WinForms to WPF and introducing the PRISM framework, which allowed for a more flexible and pluggable UI architecture

  • Helped to unify the team and create a more collaborative environment by driving initiatives to share knowledge through regular learn and share sessions, pair programming, and running book clubs on technical topics relevant to the team’s day to day challenges

items.headline: DevOps Engineer | AWS · Kubernetes · Terraform · CI/CD | AI-assisted infrastructure work with human approval gates | 99.9% uptime, ~30% fewer failed deploys | Remote
items.about:
Teams want to move faster with AI tooling and can't, because nothing in their pipeline is safe to hand to something that acts on its own. I build that missing layer: keyless authentication, hard scanning gates, immutable artifacts, human approval before production. Then I use AI agents inside it daily to ship real infrastructure work.

Seven years in software, the last four on infrastructure, reliability and delivery. AWS and GCP, Kubernetes on EKS, Terraform, and self-managed bare metal where there is no cloud provider to catch you.

How I work:

- Guardrails first. On my platform project Plinth, CI/CD runs on GitHub Actions with OIDC keyless authentication, so no long-lived cloud credentials exist anywhere. Trivy scanning is a hard gate, image tags are immutable semver+SHA, and production needs manual approval. Default-deny NetworkPolicy, least-privilege IAM, secrets in AWS Secrets Manager and never in Terraform state. These are the preconditions for letting anything automated propose infrastructure changes.

- AI-assisted, never AI-unsupervised. I use Claude Code and similar agents daily: generating and refactoring Terraform modules, drafting runbooks, speeding up log analysis during incident triage, writing pipeline configuration. Everything passes the same review, scanning and approval gates as human-written code. Agents make me faster. They don't make me skip the discipline.

- I write the context agents need. Plinth ships with 10 Architecture Decision Records, operational runbooks, networking docs and disaster recovery procedures. That documentation exists because a platform nobody else can operate isn't finished, and it is exactly what makes an agent's output useful instead of plausible-sounding noise.

- Root causes, not repeat tickets. I traced a recurring outage to container IP reassignment breaking forwarding rules after Docker restarts, then shipped a self-healing systemd service and a runbook. I rebuilt a compromised environment from scratch under time pressure, then designed the layered security model that made that class of exposure impossible.

- Measurable: 99.9% uptime across production platforms, roughly 30% fewer deployment failures through proper CI/CD, roughly 20% lower cloud spend through right-sizing and lifecycle policies.

Currently going deeper on agent-driven incident triage and evaluation, plus AWS Solutions Architect and ArgoCD.
AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner. B.Sc. Software Engineering, Daffodil International University.

Open to remote roles with US/EU overlap, and to relocation. ahmedmusa.dev@gmail.com

projects.title: Plinth: Production AWS Platform Foundation
projects.description:
A production AWS platform built end to end infrastructure through application delivery with the security gates and written decisions that let a team (or an automated tool) change it safely.

Infrastructure: five custom Terraform modules (network, EKS, ECR, RDS, monitoring) provisioning a three-tier VPC across public, private-app and private-db subnets. RDS PostgreSQL reachable only via private subnets, credentials in AWS Secrets Manager, never in Terraform state. S3-native state locking.

Delivery pipeline, built as a guardrail system: GitHub Actions with OIDC keyless authentication so no long-lived cloud credentials exist anywhere. Trivy vulnerability scanning as a hard gate on every image. Immutable semver+SHA tags so artifacts are promoted rather than rebuilt. Manual approval before production. Kustomize base plus four environment overlays (local, staging, production, CI) cluster state lives in Git as declarative manifests, so every deploy is reviewable and reversible.

Security and reliability by design: default-deny NetworkPolicy, security-group-to-security-group isolation, non-root containers with read-only root filesystems, Pod Disruption Budgets, readiness and liveness probes, CloudWatch alarms.

Application layer: Next.js 16 frontend, async FastAPI/SQLAlchemy backend, multi-stage Docker builds for amd64 and arm64.

Documentation: 10 Architecture Decision Records covering the tradeoffs behind each choice, plus networking docs, CI/CD design notes, operational runbooks and disaster recovery procedures. This is the layer that makes the platform operable by someone who isn't me and the layer that makes AI-assisted changes to it produce useful output rather than plausible guesses.

Over the past decade, I've worked with startups, SMEs, and international manufacturers across Europe, North America, and Asia, leading projects from the first sketch through engineering, supplier development, production, and market launch.
 
My experience spans industrial design, product engineering, sourcing, manufacturing, and project management. Rather than focusing on one discipline, I specialise in connecting them, ensuring that good ideas don't get lost between design, engineering, production, and commercial reality.
 
My work covers the complete product development process, from defining the product and validating concepts to coordinating engineering, manufacturing, and production.
 
Areas of expertise
 
 • Industrial Design

 • Project Management
 • Engineering Coordination
 • Design for Manufacturing (DfM)
 • Manufacturing & Supply Chain Development
 • Supplier Management

I believe successful products are built by making the right decisions early, validating assumptions, and staying involved until the work is complete. Great design is only valuable when it can be manufactured efficiently, delivered successfully, and create lasting value for the people who use it.
 
My goal is to bridge the gap between ideas, engineering, manufacturing, and execution—transforming concepts into products that are practical, manufacturable, and built to last.

Here, I managed everything from those first wild ideas to the final production-ready model.

The whole process, from concept to completion, was one big lesson in how to blend style with performance.

Building bikes that were tough, reliable, and visually striking—well, that’s what Superhuman was all about, and I loved every second of it.

Living in Shanghai, working with FLX, was my crash course in e-bike innovation.

We were a small team with big dreams, designing electric bikes that were built to go places—literally and figuratively.

I got my hands dirty with every part of the process, from the initial design sketches to the final test rides.

Seeing our bikes take off around the world was a massive thrill, and it taught me that the best work often comes from the scrappiest beginnings.

At JungleFish, I learned how design can tell a story and make a difference.

I was tasked with designing eco-friendly furniture from recycled materials, and it opened my eyes to the power of sustainability.

The experience was about creating something functional, and something that could last and have meaning.

Moving to Shanghai and diving into the design world with Design2Gather was a bold step.

Here, I worked on a mix of client-based projects, where every day meant tackling new design and engineering challenges.

From sketch to prototype, I learned the ins and outs of collaborating with clients to bring their ideas to life.

The experience gave me a hands-on approach to design—where creativity meets practical problem-solving.

It was a fast-paced environment, but every project taught me how to balance innovation with real-world application.

Working on rollercoasters at Vekoma Rides felt like a childhood dream come true.

I got to work on vehicle engineering, helping create rides that would thrill people from around the world.

It was all about combining fun with safety, and the lessons in precision and reliability still stick with me today.

Seeing my work in action, with people’s smiles and excitement, was an unforgettable reminder of the joy that great design can bring.

education.schoolName: Fontys Venlo University of Applied Sciences
education.description:
During my time at Fontys Venlo, I wasn’t just hitting the books; I was diving headfirst into the real-world challenges of industrial design. 

This degree was all about practical experience, blending classroom learning with hands-on projects rooted in actual industry problems. 

I tackled real-world projects, collaborated with industry professionals, and completed an internship and a graduation thesis that tested everything I had learned. 

This was where I built a solid foundation in design engineering, setting the stage for my future in product development.

This wasn’t your typical course—it was a crash course in building a business from the ground up. 

Together with Gabriel Costa, I navigated the entrepreneurial waters, guided by industry mentors who supported us every step of the way. 

We explored business strategy, tackled the complexities of launching a product, and faced the realities of startup life head-on. 

It was an eye-opening experience that fueled my passion for entrepreneurship and gave me the tools to bring my ideas to life.

Stepping into VIA University’s exchange program was like entering a melting pot of engineering talent. 

For five months, I immersed myself in mechanical engineering courses, collaborating with both Danish and international students. 

We learned by doing, tackling complex projects and blending different cultural perspectives into our engineering solutions. 

It was an intense and rewarding experience that broadened my technical skills and gave me a global perspective on product development.

projects.title: White Label Ebike
projects.description:
The White Label Ebike project simplifies the process for brands looking to enter the e-bike market. 

We handpicked a premium selection of e-bikes that brands can customize to fit their identity, eliminating the hassle of navigating multiple suppliers. 

This is about offering top-quality products that align perfectly with brand visions and market needs, without the usual complications.

projects.title: Studebaker.bike – A Modern Classic, Electrified
projects.description:
As Creative Director, I led the design and development of Studebaker.bike – a premium electric bicycle inspired by the timeless charm of the Studebaker legacy. The goal was to blend vintage automotive aesthetics with modern-day e-bike technology, creating a riding experience that feels both iconic and effortless.

The result is a bold, elegant e-bike built for urban riders who appreciate style, comfort, and performance.
My work included product vision, frame and component development, visual identity direction, and guiding the bike from concept to real-world launch.

Proud to see this project turning heads and bringing storytelling back into cycling.

projects.title: Toverland E-Bike – Designed for a World of Wonder
projects.description:
For the launch of the Toverland E-Bike, I worked closely with the Toverland theme park team to create a unique, branded e-bike that captures the playfulness and magic of their park experience. The goal was to design a fun, family-friendly bike that seamlessly fits into both leisure and promotional environments.

The bike features bright, glossy colors, bold frame details, and visual storytelling that connects directly to Toverland’s joyful brand. As Creative Director, I oversaw the concept, visual design language, and frame customization process to ensure it delivered both rideability and a spark of magic.

A great example of how e-bikes can go beyond function and become part of a brand’s world.

projects.title: ZAET Metro E-Bike – Built for Daily Movement
projects.description:
The ZAET Metro is our flagship e-bike platform, developed as part of ZAET’s long-term Cycle as a Service strategy. Designed for daily riders, urban fleets, and subscription-based services, the Metro combines durability, comfort, and ease of maintenance in a sleek, modular frame.

As CEO of ZAET, I led the development of this platform, from early concept and industrial design to sourcing, production, and launch strategy. Every detail of the Metro was designed with long-term use in mind, including tool-free maintenance, integrated lights, and options for cargo or fleet adaptation.

projects.title: Hybrid 2024
projects.description:
This project is where the world of trekking e-bikes meets rugged terrain. 

Built for sporty riders tackling tough paths, Hybrid 2024 is designed with a suspension fork and a 250W mid-motor, providing power and comfort. 

This isn’t just an e-bike for the office commute; it’s a ride for those who want to explore the outdoors without breaking a sweat. 

Every element of Hybrid 2024 was carefully crafted with durability and performance in mind.

projects.title: ROVER 45 -Chainless Speed Pedelec
projects.description:
Working with Look Cycles on the ROVER 45 was all about pushing design limits. 

Inspired by the brand’s unique spirit, we crafted an urban speed pedelec that’s fast, resilient, and visually striking, thanks to CIXI’s chainless technology. 

The ROVER 45 is not just a bike—it’s a celebration of freedom in geometry, integrating details that reflect the sophisticated DNA of Look Cycles.

projects.title: PINION Electric Mountain Bike
projects.description:
This EMTB was designed for thrill-seekers who live for speed and adventure. 

With a powerful 250W hub motor and Pinion Gearbox, this project marries functionality with excitement. 

It’s built for mountain bike enthusiasts who want a robust, high-performing e-bike that can handle the roughest terrains and the steepest climbs.

projects.title: ​Youth Electric Urban Bike
projects.description:
For young riders who value style and functionality, the Youth Electric Urban Bike brings a sleek design with hidden battery and integrated features like hydraulic disc brakes and internally routed cables. 

This bike is about low maintenance and high reliability, perfect for daily commutes or trips around town, built with the young commuter in mind.

projects.title: Route Urban
projects.description:
The Route Urban project with Route Assembly has been a milestone in electric mobility. 

Here, we’re blending the latest in 3D printing technology with a vision for sustainable urban commuting. 

It’s more than just an e-bike; it’s a concept designed to reshape urban transportation, with a focus on efficiency, flexibility, and groundbreaking design. 

With every print, we’re pushing boundaries to create a product that’s as versatile as it is eco-friendly.

projects.title: Kneissl Bikes
projects.description:
Partnering with Franz Kneissl, this project aimed to bring a line of e-bikes into the Austrian market through dealerships. 

We faced industry-wide component shortages but managed to secure high-quality parts like the Shimano Drivetrain and Bosch motors. 

The result was a branded Kneissl e-bike line, maintaining the brand’s reputation for quality and resilience.

projects.title: MENOMIC - 3D Printed Carbon Ebike
projects.description:
Developing the Menomic bike with Tzmann founder Andre Gotzmann was about embracing cutting-edge tech. 

Through 3D printing, we created a frame that’s perfectly tailored to individual riders. 

This project was all about innovation, translating the final concept into a functioning, rideable prototype that delivers both comfort and performance.

projects.title: WEAPON X - Full Sus Carbon E-Mtb
projects.description:
Weapon X is a powerhouse in mountain e-bikes. 

Built with a carbon fiber frame, this bike was designed for steep climbs and rough descents. 

We focused on suspension and geometry, tailoring it as an uphill-oriented enduro bike with the added weight of an e-bike in mind. 

It’s a ride built to excel in challenging environments.

projects.title: Babymaker II - Stealth Ebike
projects.description:
Developing Babymaker II was about taking an e-bike sensation to the next level. 

Building on the success of the first model, which raised over $10 million in crowdfunding, we enhanced the design and functionality for a 2022 release. 

With prototypes built and assembly in Detroit, this project brought the Babymaker series to a new level of refinement and appeal.

projects.title: BLADE 2.0 - 54Kph Ebike with a 1000W Motor
projects.description:
The Blade 2.0 was all about performance. 

This e-bike combines a powerful 52V battery and a belt-driven 1000W mid-drive motor, taking off-road adventures to new heights. 

With an intuitive Rohloff 500/14 SPEEDHUB, this bike makes shifting effortless and gives riders a smooth, robust experience that’s ideal for extreme terrain.

projects.title: Zigzag
projects.description:
Meet ZIGZAG—my graduation thesis, where traditional values and modern design come together for Chinese households. 

This project stemmed from a close collaboration between Ecquality (ECQ) and JungleFish, exploring how brand consistency and product design can be redefined in a dynamic, evolving market. 

Tasked with creating a cohesive brand language, ZIGZAG aimed to transform ECQ’s approach to product design by honing in on clarity, consistency, and culture. 

Through strategy and design, ZIGZAG brings a fresh perspective to ECQ’s product collection, setting a new standard in brand evolution and cultural resonance.

projects.title: DFES
projects.description:
This project was personal. 

Designing an exoskeleton hand for a friend who had lost function in his right arm taught me how engineering can transform lives. 

Working on this was an eye-opener in how technology and empathy intersect, as we focused on creating a practical, user-friendly solution to improve mobility.

projects.title: Coffee in the Future
projects.description:
In partnership with Philips, we explored sustainable design by creating a coffee machine that generates purified water from polluted air. 

Aimed at humid regions like southern China, this project tied sustainability with functionality, addressing real-world challenges and embracing Philips' vision for a healthier future.

items.about:
Freije Quality Engineering is a Verified Veteran Owned full-service consulting firm providing clients with quality system and regulatory affairs consulting.  Including implementation of the new European Medical Device Regulation (EU 2017/745).

Over 35 years experience working for the government and the private sector, with over 27 years in the medical device and pharmaceutical industries.  Experience includes supporting quality systems and various product lines at Roche Diagnostics, supported projects for the Special Forces and Direct Fire Control at Raytheon Technical Services Company, various Engineering and Quality positions with increasing responsibilities at Eli Lilly and Company supporting medical device commercialization, device quality, device manufacturing, and bulk manufacturing for injectables and dry products manufacturing for clinical trials.

Honorably discharged after serving eight years in the US Army as a Systems Mechanic.

John’s major contribution was working with suppliers and customers to ensure critical quality requirements were flowed down and met.  Within six months of employment John worked with the customer to accept approximately $6M worth of product as well as modifying the design while still ensuring safe operations for the military.  He also led improvement efforts on a project to help identify and reduce cost of quality by 50% on a major international client.

John held several positions with increasing responsibilities at Eli Lilly and Company ranging from Process Engineer to Quality Engineer working in Lilly’s pharmaceutical manufacturing and medical device divisions.  John’s duties ranged from supporting solid dose manufacturing to commercialization of medical devices as well on ongoing supplier management though the development and maintenance of supplier quality agreements.  John's key contributions focused around working with key suppliers to help reduce medical device complaints by facilitating root cause analysis and implementing effective corrective actions. publications.title: LLooMA: A Network-Native Orchestration Architecture
publications.description:
LLooMA (Low-Latency Orchestration of Models and Agents) is a network-native architecture for distributed language intelligence. Rather than existing as a model with static weights, LLooMA operates as an orchestration policy that dynamically decomposes requests, coordinates execution across decentralized hosts, and synthesizes results into a single coherent response.

The system introduces a new paradigm—intelligent scaling—in which performance improves not by increasing model size or hardware alone, but by optimizing how computation is structured, routed, and executed across the network. By combining deterministic orchestration, dual-host racing, latency enforcement, and seamless continuation fallback, LLooMA delivers reliable, low-latency responses despite operating over unreliable, heterogeneous infrastructure.

In doing so, LLooMA reframes AI systems from monolithic artifacts into adaptive execution processes, bridging centralized intelligence with decentralized compute.

publications.title: PeerLLM: A Manifesto for a Decentralized AI Economy
publications.description: The PeerLLM Whitepaper outlines a vision for a decentralized AI economy where individuals, not corporations, own and benefit from AI infrastructure. It introduces a peer-to-peer network that allows anyone to host AI models, share data, and contribute computing power in exchange for rewards. By distributing AI processing across independent hosts through an orchestrated system of consumers, networks, and providers, PeerLLM aims to democratize access to artificial intelligence, enhance privacy, and reduce centralization of power in the AI industry.

Here's the thesis: Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, and Codex are incredible for solo developers. At team scale they break down. Context loss between sessions. Intent drift between developer and AI. Merge conflicts when multiple agents code in parallel. Clients with zero visibility into what's getting built. Spec Kitty fixes that. Persistent specs as a source of truth. Worktree isolation for parallel work. A read-only client dashboard for spec approval and progress. AI guardrails. Code stays local, only workflow metadata syncs to the cloud. Built for engineering teams of 5 to 500+.

Outside Spec Kitty, I run B2B SaaS growth strategy for founders and leadership teams.

B2B growth doesn't stall because teams aren't working hard. It stalls because strategy, demand, and technology aren't aligned around how buyers actually decide. I help B2B companies scale smarter by aligning brand positioning, demand generation, and AI-enabled GTM systems around the buyer's actual journey. 15+ years across SaaS, health and fitness, finance, and manufacturing.

Track record:

• Author of "Ranked and Cited" (2026), "Authentic Marketing in the Age of AI" (2023), and "AUTHENTICITY: Marketing to Generation Z" (2022)
• CEO of Strategic eMarketing for 15+ years
• Host of the "Marketing in the Age of AI" podcast
• Co-Founder, priivacy.ai
• Board member, Jack and Buena Hazard Foundation

If you're an engineering leader scaling AI coding, demo and early access at spec-kitty.ai. If you're a B2B SaaS founder hitting a growth plateau, DM me here.

experience.position: Author-The 7 Principles of the Magic Rock: How Solitude in Nature Anchors Your Mental Health
experience.description:
In an era where digital overload and the mental health crisis intersect, Emanuel Rose offers a sanctuary through his unique Magic Rock principles. From personal experiences, scientific research, and a deep reverence for the natural world, Rose presents a compelling case for the healing and grounding effects of time spent in solitude amidst nature.

The book is divided into chapters that delve into the heart of Rose’s philosophy, exploring the critical aspects of connecting with nature, such as preparation, immersion, and the art of unplugging from the digital world. Each chapter is a step towards understanding how intentional solitude can lead to profound self-discovery, creative rejuvenation, and a renewed sense of purpose.

“The 7 Principles of the Magic Rock” is more than just a guide; it’s an invitation to embark on a journey of self-reflection to rediscover the joy and tranquility that nature offers. It challenges readers to embrace solitude as a path to inner peace and encourages them to find their own ‘Magic Rock’ – a space where they can connect with their innermost thoughts and the timeless wisdom of the natural world.

Embrace this journey with Emanuel Rose and discover how solitude in nature can be the anchor you need for a balanced and fulfilled life.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: AI Simplified
receivedRecommendations.description:
Hey, I’m Jonathan Green, host of the Artificial Intelligence Podcast, and I want to talk about my experience with Emanuel Rose.

Emanuel is one of the most thoughtful and authentic voices when it comes to using AI in marketing. His approach to blending AI’s capabilities with human creativity is refreshing, especially in a time when many rush to automate everything without a clear plan. Emanuel’s ability to maintain authenticity while leveraging AI to streamline processes and enhance content creation is remarkable.

During our podcast conversation, I was struck by his deep understanding of how AI can be used to empower marketers without losing their unique voice. He emphasized the importance of keeping your content personal by training AI on your own work, which helps it reflect your voice rather than diluting it. His insight into how AI can be used for tasks like summarizing and organizing data, while still keeping human creativity at the forefront, was both practical and inspiring.

What excites me about Emanuel is his commitment to doing things the right way—not just jumping on trends, but thinking critically about how to use AI ethically and effectively. He’s someone I look forward to learning more from as the AI landscape evolves.
